transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Well, I suppose the main thing is my sleep. It’s gotten… pretty unsettled, I guess. At first I’d wake after two or three hours and feel strangely ready to get going, like I should be drafting plans or sorting things out. I didn’t think too much of it at the time.

But now it’s less useful, if that makes sense. I’m lying awake before dawn with my stomach tight, and I don’t really feel rested. I’m not sure if that’s the right sort of thing to come in for, but it’s been troubling me.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things the way you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but things I usually care about just don’t seem to reach me lately.

I used to spend whole afternoons at the museum, or get absorbed in photography, cooking, even bridge. Now I’ll look at my camera or think about sitting at the bridge table, and I just feel… nothing, really. Mostly I notice how much effort it would take to pretend I’m enjoying it. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to be concerned?

I’m not sure I’d call it worrying, exactly. I mean… I think about things, of course, but not always with a clear reason. Sometimes I just feel uneasy and then look for something to attach it to, if that makes sense.

I don’t want to overstate it. It’s more like a background hum than one particular concern. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling fatigued or lacking in energy most days, even when you haven’t done anything particularly taxing?

I’m not sure I’d say fatigued exactly… I mean, I’m older, so some slowing down seems expected, doesn’t it?

There are days I don’t feel especially energetic, but I haven’t really been keeping track of whether it’s most days. I suppose I notice myself sitting longer before getting up to do things, but I don’t know if that counts.
Would you say you feel down or sad most of the time lately, even when there’s no particular reason for it?

I don’t know that I’d say “most of the time.” I mean, I have low moments, certainly, but I try not to sit around labeling myself as sad, if that makes sense.

Some days feel a bit heavier than others, but I’m not sure there’s always a clear reason. I may just be… quieter, maybe. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you been feeling like you’re not worth much or that you’re letting people down, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

I suppose… yes, there is some of that. I don’t like saying it that way, because it sounds rather dramatic.

But I do keep going back over that investment decision in my head, again and again. I tell myself I’ve put my wife’s security at risk, and that after a lifetime of trying to be the responsible one, I’ve made a fool of myself. I know you’re probably asking whether it feels bigger than the facts warrant… and maybe it does. But it’s hard not to feel I’ve let her down.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in those activities, like photography or bridge, or is there still a part of you that wants to engage but just can’t seem to make yourself do it?

I suppose it’s more than just not getting around to it, if I’m being honest.

I used to spend whole afternoons at the museum, or get completely absorbed in taking photographs or cooking something. And now… I’ll look at the camera, or think about sitting down for bridge, and there’s just nothing there. Not even much pleasure at the thought of it—mostly it feels like effort, like I’d have to pretend to be interested.

I don’t know if that’s the right way to describe it, but yes, it does feel like I’ve lost that part of it.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless or unable to sit still lately?

I hadn’t quite thought of it that way, but… yes, I suppose there has been some of that.

My wife notices it more than I do. She’ll say I’m pacing around the house, sort of shuffling papers as if I’m late for some board meeting, which sounds a bit absurd now that I’m saying it. And then other times I’ll just sit at the kitchen table very still, and she has to wait because it takes me longer than it should to answer a simple question.

I don’t mean to make too much of it, but yes, I think there’s been a change.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately? For instance, have you been eating less than usual or lost weight without trying?

Not especially, no… at least I don’t think so.

My appetite may not be quite what it was, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it. I’m still eating meals when they’re put in front of me. I haven’t been weighing myself regularly, so I couldn’t honestly say there’s been any real weight loss. Nothing I’ve noticed in a clear way, if that helps.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in activities like photography or bridge, or is there still a part of you that wants to engage but just can’t seem to make yourself do it?

Yes… I think it’s closer to having lost the interest, if that’s the right way to put it.

I used to spend whole afternoons at the museum, or lose myself in photography or cooking without even noticing the time. Now I’ll look at the camera, or think about a bridge game, and there’s just… nothing much there. Mostly I think about how much effort it would take to act as if I’m enjoying it.

I don’t mean that to sound dramatic, but that’s probably the honest answer.

Have you had any period lasting several days where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you felt extremely energetic—even to the point where people around you noticed a change in your behavior?

Yes… I think there was a period like that. I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but for a few weeks I felt unusually… capable, I suppose. Almost brilliantly optimistic, like every obstacle was minor and I could see the obvious solution to everything.

The less flattering part is that if someone questioned me, I didn’t take it well. I could snap at them, as if they were trying to interfere or sabotage things, when really they were probably just asking ordinary questions. My wife noticed it, certainly. I thought at the time I was just being decisive, but looking back… yes, it was a noticeable change.
How long did that period of unusually high mood and increased energy last?

It lasted longer than I’d like to admit, honestly.

Not just a few days. I suppose… about five months, after the investment loss. I kept telling myself I was just being practical, trying to fix what had happened, but looking back, I wasn’t really living like my usual retired self. Everything seemed to revolve around undoing the damage.

That’s probably the fairest way to put it, if that makes sense.
